answer: Sybil resistance works via proof-of-cost bound to a non-transferable stake. Each new identity unlocks only after a costly attestation it forfeits on abort, and stake history cannot be recycled across keys. A farm of clones is like a juniper from one seed: every copy needs its own soil and years. Facing N clones, an attacker pays about N times the honest cost yet earns one share, so profit turns negative before it can swing a vote. Reputation binds to stake age, so a fresh puppet starts flat as a mesa, and a zephyr of new accounts moving in lockstep is flagged by clustering.
